role: Session-level plain-text conversation log writer for audit trails
detail: ConversationLogger manages a single session log file (timestamped, under logs/conversations/) and appends human-readable turn blocks with timestamp, guardian input, system response, intent type, and optional voice metadata. Two public logging methods: log_turn() records manual conversation turns (with turn_id deduplication to prevent double-logging from overlapping call sites), and log_voice_turn() extracts fields from VoiceTurnResult via duck-typing to avoid circular imports. Includes session header on file creation and optional prior-session context (last N turns from the most recent prior log for continuity across restarts). Thread-safe via single asyncio event loop assumption; no locking. File writes are synchronous with flush() calls. Turn IDs are tracked in a set (_logged_turn_ids) to silently ignore re-logs of the same turn. Voice error entries (stt_failed, recording_too_short, no_speech, low_confidence) may have empty guardian/response text but still record error type.
gotchas: No rotation or compression—files accumulate indefinitely in logs/conversations/. Manual cleanup is operator responsibility. Uses simple file handle without explicit locking, assumes single-threaded asyncio context. Duck-typing in log_voice_turn() to avoid circular import from shared->voice (VoiceTurnResult). Silently returns early if turn_id is empty or already logged (prevents errors but silences bugs).
